doc: Corpora registers the engine capabilities praxis's sequence scripts invoke on it. Each capability names a corpora CLI verb and declares the argument shape praxis must build; praxis's engine resolver composes the argv from this data and calls the verb generically, without ever hardcoding a corpora verb string or learning what a verb means. This is the write-verb analogue of the handoff plugin manifest -- the whole engine-write coupling surface reduced to one declarative file. A second engine could drop its own manifest declaring its own capability->verb map; praxis core would resolve against it identically. Arg descriptors: `flag` + value by default; `positional: true` emits the value alone; `global: true` places the pair BEFORE the verb (corpora's `--root` is a global option that precedes the subcommand); `boolean: true` emits just the flag when the param is truthy. A `required` arg missing from the params raises before the engine is touched.

cli.doc: Where corpora's CLI lives. `entry` is resolved relative to THIS manifest file, so when a project imports this contribution into praxis's engine slot the location travels with it. Praxis reads this to learn where to invoke; it never encodes corpus.py's path itself.

capabilities.desc: give me the domain set for unit-of-work U at root R (returns JSON on stdout)

bootstrap a project by writing corpora/config.md — the engine's own bootstrap, the symmetric counterpart to praxis_init's root marker; praxis's session-entry invokes it when a root is not yet bootstrapped

emit the engine-contributed parts of a spawn prompt (stance frame, domain bodies, handoff-read schema) plus any composition problems, as JSON on stdout — praxis composes these into its prompt skeleton without knowing what a part means (the handoff-plugin pattern for spawn prompts)
write a freshly-authored or mined ratified principle into a domain
write an entry already queued in the import-candidates file back as ratified
create an empty domain container (frontmatter only) from a source domain file, so a plugin's judgment face can be staged into a project that doesn't have the domain yet
propose one principle/convention from a source domains-dir as a candidate

propose every principle+convention from every source domain (shape-matched batch), staged as candidates for the ratify gate — this is how a plugin's judgment face enters a project without bypassing the gate. Re-invocation is a sync: source-side edits of already-present ids queue as update candidates, source-side kills of entries still live in the project as kill candidates, both still gate-mediated
browse a source domains-dir's principles+conventions, read-only, proposes nothing
run every schema migration between the pool's schema-version stamp and current, in order, and re-stamp config.md — the first step of phases/pool-sync.md; idempotent
one-time per pool: move every working file's killed: entries into the audit file's kill log (kills live in audit since 2026-08-07; working files keep an empty killed: marker)

move a domain's working file AND its whole audit trail (provenance + counter + efficacy) from one domains-dir to another — the scripted form of a plugin extraction's audit surgery; pure mechanics, no judgment about what should move
one-time: materialize a pre-dissolution project's effective domain set
measure the materialized domain set (read after migrate)
verify the materialized domain set matches its audit; a hard migration gate
record a ratify-gate counter update for a domain (fired/violated/idle, drift)
emit the maintenance triggers due for the project, read-only
